source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Focusing only on medication management, with fairly little exercise component actually built into the overall program design","B":"Resting on fairly little established evidence of benefit despite being a commonly recommended intervention for this population","C":"Structured exercise training, education, and psychosocial support, shown to improve functional capacity and quality of life in chronic respiratory disease","D":"Being relevant mainly for clients with the most severe form of the disease, rather than for COPD clients across the disease spectrum"}}
source_row.rationale: Pulmonary rehabilitation programs typically include structured exercise training, disease-specific education, and psychosocial support, shown in strong evidence to improve functional capacity and quality of life across a range of chronic respiratory disease severity, not only the most advanced cases.
source_row.source_detail: Components and Benefits of Pulmonary Rehabilitation
source_row.source_name: American Thoracic Society — Pulmonary Rehabilitation Guidelines
